evaluate_progressive_tax_amount_and_subs.intent: Evaluate whether a claimed tax amount and cited subsection agree with the applicable progressive tax bracket in the current source, returning the native binary label.
evaluate_progressive_tax_amount_and_subs.procedure:
def apply(inputs, premises):
    income = float(inputs["taxable_income"])
    actual_tax = 0.0
    actual_subsection = ""
    found = False
    for i in range(len(inputs["bracket_upper_bounds"])):
        if not found and income <= float(inputs["bracket_upper_bounds"][i]):
            actual_tax = float(inputs["bracket_base_amounts"][i]) + float(inputs["bracket_rates"][i]) * (income - float(inputs["bracket_thresholds"][i]))
            actual_subsection = str(inputs["bracket_labels"][i])
            found = True
    actual_tax = round(actual_tax, 2)
    amount_ok = abs(actual_tax - float(inputs["asserted_tax"])) <= 0.005
    subsection_ok = actual_subsection == str(inputs["asserted_subsection"])
    answer = "Contradiction"
    if found and amount_ok and subsection_ok:
        answer = "Entailment"
    return {"answer": answer}

raw_block.rationale: Create an airline totaler that avoids the previously unresolved route-table field by having one joint reader classify every current item and return aligned per-item base, overweight, and oversize fees. The deterministic helper applies the higher-of excess-fee rule and adds the ticket price.

skill.intent: Compute the exact integer ticket price plus all current bag fees from aligned per-item checked-bag, overweight, and oversize fee assessments.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What is the current passenger's integer ticket price?

inputs.name: bag_checked_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in its stated order, what base checked-bag fee applies after using the permitted personal-item and carry-on allowances and assigning checked-bag ordinal positions? Return zero for an item carried without a checked-bag fee.

inputs.name: bag_overweight_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in the same order, what overweight fee applies under the current route, cabin, weight allowance, and weight band? Return zero when no overweight fee applies.

inputs.name: bag_oversize_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in the same order, what oversize fee applies from its summed outside dimensions and the current route's size bands? Return zero when no oversize fee applies.

outputs.name: answer
outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus all applicable fees for every current bag.

premises.name: combined_excess_fee_rule
premises.question: When the same bag is both overweight and oversize, which excess fee is added to its checked-bag fee?

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

reads.question: Using the current itinerary, cabin, bag order, dimensions, weights, allowances, and fee tables, classify every item and return aligned base checked, overweight, and oversize fees.

raw_block.rationale: Create a narrow Illinois helper for the trigger failure: it applies the state’s residual personal-property exemption, preserves exact asset names, and emits either citation-only or citation-and-value native mappings.

inputs.question: For each current asset, is it personal rather than business property and within Illinois's residual category of any other property rather than a more specific listed category?

inputs.name: output_family
inputs.question: Does the current output contract require citation arrays (EC) or citation-and-claim-value records (EV)?

raw_block.rationale: Create a generic OpenExempt formatter that reads a flat, current-source claim record, preserves exact asset descriptions and literal citations, and emits either native EC or EV output. inputs.name: asset_names
inputs.question: What are the exact asset descriptions appearing in the current Facts, without ownership or valuation wording?

inputs.name: asset_values
inputs.question: What dollar value belongs to each current asset in the same order?

inputs.name: claim_asset_indexes
inputs.question: For every exemption applicable under the already-determined governing exemption systems, what zero-based current-asset index does the claim concern? Repeat an index when multiple exemptions apply.

inputs.name: claim_citations
inputs.question: In the same order, what literal statutory citation string identifies each applicable exemption? Include only the specific exemption citations required by the current output contract, not enabling or definitional provisions.

inputs.name: claim_limits
inputs.question: In the same order, what maximum dollar amount can be protected for each asset-exemption pair when considered independently under the current contract? For an unlimited exemption, use the corresponding asset's full value.

inputs.name: output_family
inputs.question: Does the current response schema require citation arrays (EC) or citation-and-claim-value records (EV)?

raw_block.rationale: Create an airline terminal helper around one coupled per-item assessment. Parallel arrays retain bag order and force the source reader to account for carried-item allowances, complimentary checked bags, checked ordinals, route, cabin, weight allowance, and size band before deterministic aggregation.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: bag_base_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in stated order, what base checked-bag fee applies after using the one-personal-item and one-carry-on allowances and applying route, cabin, complimentary-bag benefits, and checked ordinal? Return zero for a carried or complimentary item.

inputs.name: bag_overweight_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in the same order, what overweight fee applies after using the standard weight allowance for that particular checked position, including any higher allowance limited to complimentary First or Business bags? Return zero where none applies.

inputs.name: bag_oversize_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in the same order, what oversize fee applies after adding its length, width, and height and selecting the current route's size band? Return zero where none applies.

skill.intent: Calculate the exact integer ticket price plus all current bag fees from aligned per-item base, overweight, and oversize assessments.

raw_block.rationale: Create a compact airline terminal helper around one coupled per-item assessment. Asking for each item's final fee keeps carry-on allocation, checked ordinal, cabin benefits, and the higher-of excess rule aligned, avoiding the repeated missing-field failures of wider schedule readers.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: per_item_final_bag_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in stated order, what final bag fee applies after allocating the permitted carried item, assigning checked-bag ordinal and cabin benefits, and adding the higher of any overweight or oversize charge? Return zero for an item carried without charge.

skill.intent: Return the exact integer ticket price plus the final applicable fee for every current bag.

outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus all applicable fees for every current bag.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: ticket_price
fields.question: What ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

fields.name: per_item_final_bag_fees
fields.question: What complete fee applies to each current item in order, using zero for an item carried without charge?

reads.question: Jointly assess the current ordered items under the itinerary's carry-on allowance, cabin benefits, checked-bag schedule, weight bands, size bands, and combined-excess rule.

origin.quote: You can bring only one carry-on item along with your personal item.

source_obligations.statement: Use no more than the permitted carry-on allowance before assigning checked-bag positions to the remaining items.

origin.quote: 1st and 2nd checked bags are complimentary for:

source_obligations.statement: Apply the current route, cabin, complimentary benefits, and checked ordinal when determining each item's base fee.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

source_obligations.statement: When one checked bag is both overweight and oversize, include only the higher excess fee in addition to its checked-bag fee.

source_provenance.quote: The total size of your carry-on, including the handles and wheels, cannot exceed 22 x 14 x 9 inches (56 x 36 x 23 cm) and must fit in the sizer at the airport.
We calculate the size limits of your bag by adding the total outside dimensions of each bag, length + width + height.
More than one fee may apply per bag that exceeds standard dimensions for both weight and size. The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

raw_block.rationale: Offer a coordinated airline alternative with a genuine producer–terminal dependency. One joint reader preserves alignment among base, overweight, and oversize components; the terminal helper deterministically applies the source's higher-of rule and sums the ticket total.

raw_block.rationale: Create a compact terminal helper around one coupled current-source assessment. Earlier airline drafts repeatedly failed because related fee components were requested separately or left unresolved; this reader asks for the complete bag-fee subtotal while preserving the ticket price as a distinct fact.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: baggage_fee_subtotal
inputs.question: What is the complete integer baggage-fee subtotal for all current items, excluding the ticket price, after applying the personal-item and carry-on limits, checked-bag ordinal fees, cabin and route benefits, weight allowances, overweight bands, summed-dimension oversize bands, and the higher-only rule for simultaneous overweight and oversize charges?

skill.intent: Return the exact integer ticket price plus the complete baggage-fee subtotal for the current itinerary.

outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus all applicable fees for every current bag.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: ticket_price
fields.question: What ticket price is stated in the current facts?

fields.name: baggage_fee_subtotal
fields.question: What total baggage fees apply to all current items before adding the ticket price?

reads.question: Assess the current passenger's ordered items and applicable baggage rules as one coupled record, returning the stated ticket price and the complete fee subtotal excluding that ticket price.
reads.source_locator: current RuleArena Airline source_text, facts, and question

origin.quote: You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.

source_obligations.statement: Apply at most one qualifying personal-item allowance and one qualifying carry-on allowance before assigning successive checked-bag positions.

origin.quote: All published bag fees apply at each check-in location and are base rates according to travel dates and destination; applicable taxes are not shown.

source_obligations.statement: Apply the current route, cabin, complimentary-bag benefits, ordinal checked fees, weight allowances, and summed-dimension oversize bands to every checked item.

raw_block.rationale: Preserve item-level auditability while avoiding the missing parallel-array failures seen in earlier drafts. A single joint reader returns one final fee per current item, and the helper performs only stable integer aggregation.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: per_item_final_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in stated order, what final fee applies after allocating only the dimensional allowances the item qualifies for, assigning remaining items successive checked positions, applying the exact route-and-cabin base schedule and complimentary benefits, applying the applicable checked-bag weight allowance and excess bands, summing outside dimensions for oversize bands, and using only the higher simultaneous overweight or oversize fee? Return zero for an item carried without charge.

skill.intent: Return the exact integer ticket price plus one jointly assessed final fee for each current item.

outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus all final per-item baggage fees.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: per_item_final_fees
fields.question: What complete fee applies to each current item in order, using zero for an item carried without charge?

origin.quote: All bag fees are non-refundable and apply per person, each way, even if you buy or get an upgrade that includes free checked bags.

source_obligations.statement: Assign checked-bag ordinals only after carried items are allocated, then apply the current route, cabin, and complimentary-bag rules to those positions.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

raw_block.rationale: Offer a middle-granularity alternative that remembers the two legal stages most often confused in prior reads: positional base fees and excess-condition fees. Both totals are acquired by one coupled reader, then combined deterministically with the ticket price.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: checked_base_fee_total
inputs.question: What is the aggregate base checked-bag fee for all current items after applying qualifying carried-item allowances, checked ordinals, the current route and cabin, and all applicable complimentary-bag benefits, but before overweight or oversize charges?

inputs.name: excess_fee_total
inputs.question: What is the aggregate excess-condition fee for all current checked items after applying the correct weight allowance and overweight band to each checked position, summing each item's outside dimensions for its oversize band, and selecting only the higher overweight or oversize fee for each item?

skill.intent: Calculate the exact integer total from the ticket price, aggregate checked-bag base fees, and aggregate higher-only excess fees.

outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus aggregate base and excess baggage fees.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: ticket_price
fields.question: What ticket price is stated?

fields.name: checked_base_fee_total
fields.question: What aggregate base checked-bag fees apply before weight and size charges?

fields.name: excess_fee_total
fields.question: What aggregate higher-only overweight or oversize charges apply?

reads.question: Assess the current ordered bags and applicable source tables together, separating the complete checked-bag base-fee total from the complete higher-only excess-fee total.

origin.quote: Main Plus includes 1 extra free checked bag in addition to the Main Cabin allowance (max of 2).

source_obligations.statement: After allocating qualifying carried items, total the base fees for successive checked positions under the current route, cabin, and complimentary-bag rules.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

source_obligations.statement: For each checked item, determine its overweight and oversize charges and include only the higher one in the aggregate excess-fee total.

source_provenance.quote: You can bring only one carry-on item along with your personal item.
We calculate the size limits of your bag by adding the total outside dimensions of each bag, length + width + height.
More than one fee may apply per bag that exceeds standard dimensions for both weight and size. The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

raw_block.rationale: Create a narrowly scoped helper for section 152(b)(1). The current rule turns on whether the individual is a dependent of a taxpayer; a qualifying child is a dependent, so the helper can evaluate the positive applicability claim from one current-facts boolean without encoding names or case answers.

inputs.name: individual_is_dependent_of_a_taxpayer
inputs.question: Do the current facts establish that the individual addressed by the proposition is a dependent of a taxpayer for the relevant taxable year, including by being that taxpayer's qualifying child or qualifying relative?

skill.intent: Determine whether a positive claim that section 152(b)(1) applies to the current individual is supported because the individual is a dependent of a taxpayer for the relevant year.

outputs.description: The native label Entailment when section 152(b)(1) applies to the individual, otherwise Contradiction.
outputs.name: answer

support.text: (c) Standard deduction
(5) Limitation on basic standard deduction in the case of certain dependents

In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under section 151 is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall not exceed the greater of-
(B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income.
(6) Certain individuals, etc., not eligible for standard deduction
In the case of-
(A) a married individual filing a separate return where either spouse itemizes deductions,
(B) a nonresident alien individual, or
(D) an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership,
the standard deduction shall be zero.
(7) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025
In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026-
Paragraph (2) shall be applied-
(i) by substituting "$18,000" for "$4,400" in subparagraph (B), and
(ii) by substituting "$12,000" for "$3,000" in subparagraph (C).
(d) Itemized deductions
For purposes of this subtitle, the term "itemized deductions" means the deductions allowable under this chapter other than-
(1) the deductions allowable in arriving at adjusted gross income, and
(2) the deduction for personal exemptions provided by section 151.
(f) Aged or blind additional amounts
(1) Additional amounts for the aged
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he has attained age 65 before the close of his taxable year, and

(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse has attained age 65 before the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
(2) Additional amount for blind
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he is blind at the close of the taxable year, and
(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse is blind as of the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
For purposes of subparagraph (B), if the spouse dies during the taxable year the determination of whether such spouse is blind shall be made as of the time of such death.
(3) Higher amount for certain unmarried individuals
In the case of an individual who is not married and is not a surviving spouse, paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be applied by substituting "$750" for "$600".
(g) Marital status
For purposes of this section, marital status shall be determined under section 7703.

{"151": "§151. Allowance of deductions for personal exemptions

(a) Allowance of deductions

In the case of an individual, the exemptions provided by this section shall be allowed as deductions in computing taxable income.

(b) Taxpayer and spouse

An exemption of the exemption amount for the taxpayer; and an additional exemption of the exemption amount for the spouse of the taxpayer if a joint return is not made by the taxpayer and his spouse, and if the spouse, for the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins, has no gross income and is not the dependent of another taxpayer.

(c) Additional exemption for dependents

An exemption of the exemption amount for each individual who is a dependent (as defined in section 152) of the taxpayer for the taxable year.

(d) Exemption amount

For purposes of this section-

    (1) In general

    Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the term "exemption amount" means $2,000.

    (2) Exemption amount disallowed in case of certain dependents

    In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under this section is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the exemption amount applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall be zero.

    (3) Phaseout

        (A) In general

        In the case of any taxpayer whose adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b), the exemption amount shall be reduced by the applicable percentage.

        (B) Applicable percentage

        For purposes of subparagraph (A), the term "applicable percentage" means 2 percentage points for each $2,500 (or fraction thereof) by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b). In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, the preceding sentence shall be applied by substituting "$1,250" for "$2,500". In no event shall the applicable percentage exceed 100 percent.

    (5) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025

    In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026, the term "exemption amount" means zero.
", "2": "§2. Definitions and special rules

(a) Definition of surviving spouse

    (1) In general

    For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer-

        (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and

        (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151.

    For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual.

    (2) Limitations

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse-

        (A) if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, or

        (B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien.

(b) Definition of head of household

    (1) In general

    An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either-

        (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of-

            (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child-

                (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and

                (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or

            (ii) any other person who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such person under section 151, or

        (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151.

    For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual.

    (2) Determination of status

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1),

        (A) an individual who is legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married;

        (B) a taxpayer shall be considered as not married at the close of his taxable year if at any time during the taxable year his spouse is a nonresident alien; and

        (C) a taxpayer shall be considered as married at the close of his taxable year if his spouse (other than a spouse described in subparagraph (B)) died during the taxable year.

    (3) Limitations

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of this subtitle a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a head of a household-

        (A) if at any time during the taxable year he is a nonresident alien; or

        (B) by reason of an individual who would not be a dependent for the taxable year but for subparagraph (H) of section 152(d)(2).
", "7703": "§7703. Determination of marital status

(a) General rule

    (1) the determination of whether an individual is married shall be made as of the close of his taxable year; except that if his spouse dies during his taxable year such determination shall be made as of the time of such death; and

    (2) an individual legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married.

(b) Certain married individuals living apart

For purposes of those provisions of this title which refer to this subsection, if-

    (1) an individual who is married (within the meaning of subsection (a)) and who files a separate return maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of the taxable year the principal place of abode of a child with respect to whom such individual is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151,

    (2) such individual furnishes over one-half of the cost of maintaining such household during the taxable year, and

    (3) during the last 6 months of the taxable year, such individual's spouse is not a member of such household,

such individual shall not be considered as married.
"}

Section 63(c)(5) applies to Bob's basic standard deduction in 2017.

support.text: (c) Standard deduction
(5) Limitation on basic standard deduction in the case of certain dependents

In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under section 151 is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall not exceed the greater of-
(B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income.
(6) Certain individuals, etc., not eligible for standard deduction
In the case of-
(A) a married individual filing a separate return where either spouse itemizes deductions,
(B) a nonresident alien individual, or
(D) an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership,
the standard deduction shall be zero.
(7) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025
In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026-
Paragraph (2) shall be applied-
(i) by substituting "$18,000" for "$4,400" in subparagraph (B), and
(ii) by substituting "$12,000" for "$3,000" in subparagraph (C).
(d) Itemized deductions
For purposes of this subtitle, the term "itemized deductions" means the deductions allowable under this chapter other than-
(1) the deductions allowable in arriving at adjusted gross income, and
(2) the deduction for personal exemptions provided by section 151.
(f) Aged or blind additional amounts
(1) Additional amounts for the aged
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he has attained age 65 before the close of his taxable year, and

(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse has attained age 65 before the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
(2) Additional amount for blind
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he is blind at the close of the taxable year, and
(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse is blind as of the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
For purposes of subparagraph (B), if the spouse dies during the taxable year the determination of whether such spouse is blind shall be made as of the time of such death.
(3) Higher amount for certain unmarried individuals
In the case of an individual who is not married and is not a surviving spouse, paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be applied by substituting "$750" for "$600".
(g) Marital status
For purposes of this section, marital status shall be determined under section 7703.

{"151": "§151. Allowance of deductions for personal exemptions

(a) Allowance of deductions

In the case of an individual, the exemptions provided by this section shall be allowed as deductions in computing taxable income.

(b) Taxpayer and spouse

An exemption of the exemption amount for the taxpayer; and an additional exemption of the exemption amount for the spouse of the taxpayer if a joint return is not made by the taxpayer and his spouse, and if the spouse, for the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins, has no gross income and is not the dependent of another taxpayer.

(c) Additional exemption for dependents

An exemption of the exemption amount for each individual who is a dependent (as defined in section 152) of the taxpayer for the taxable year.

(d) Exemption amount

For purposes of this section-

    (1) In general

    Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the term "exemption amount" means $2,000.

    (2) Exemption amount disallowed in case of certain dependents

    In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under this section is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the exemption amount applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall be zero.

    (3) Phaseout

        (A) In general

        In the case of any taxpayer whose adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b), the exemption amount shall be reduced by the applicable percentage.

        (B) Applicable percentage

        For purposes of subparagraph (A), the term "applicable percentage" means 2 percentage points for each $2,500 (or fraction thereof) by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b). In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, the preceding sentence shall be applied by substituting "$1,250" for "$2,500". In no event shall the applicable percentage exceed 100 percent.

    (5) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025

    In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026, the term "exemption amount" means zero.
", "2": "§2. Definitions and special rules

(a) Definition of surviving spouse

    (1) In general

    For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer-

        (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and

        (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151.

    For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual.

    (2) Limitations

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse-

        (A) if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, or

        (B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien.

(b) Definition of head of household

    (1) In general

    An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either-

        (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of-

            (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child-

                (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and

                (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or

        (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151.

raw_block.rationale: Create a compact airline terminal helper around one coupled current-source assessment of final per-item fees. Keeping the fees aligned by item preserves checked-bag ordinal effects and lets the deterministic program perform only the final summation.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: per_item_final_bag_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in stated order, what final bag fee applies after allocating the personal-item and carry-on allowances only to qualifying items, assigning the remaining items successive checked positions, applying route, cabin and complimentary benefits, applying the correct weight allowance and overweight band, summing outside dimensions for the oversize band, and adding only the higher simultaneous overweight or oversize fee? Return zero for an item carried without charge.

skill.intent: Return the exact integer ticket price plus the final applicable fee for every current bag.

outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus all applicable fees for every current bag.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: ticket_price
fields.question: What ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

fields.name: per_item_final_bag_fees
fields.question: What complete fee applies to each current item in order, using zero for an item carried without charge?

reads.question: Jointly classify and price every current item under the applicable carried-item allowances, checked-bag positions, route, cabin, complimentary benefits, weight rules, and size rules while preserving item order.
reads.source_locator: current RuleArena Airline source_text, facts, and question

origin.quote: You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.

source_obligations.statement: Allocate no more than one qualifying personal item and one qualifying carry-on before assigning checked-bag positions.

origin.quote:
1st and 2nd checked bags are complimentary for:
* AAdvantage Platinum® status
* oneworld® Sapphire members
* Confirmed Domestic First customers
* Confirmed Business customers
* Confirmed Premium Economy customers

source_obligations.statement: For each remaining item, apply its successive checked position together with the current route, cabin, and complimentary-bag benefits.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

source_obligations.statement: For each checked item that is both overweight and oversize, add only the higher excess fee to its checked-bag fee.

source_provenance.quote: The total size of your carry-on, including the handles and wheels, cannot exceed 22 x 14 x 9 inches (56 x 36 x 23 cm) and must fit in the sizer at the airport.
For First / Business, weight is 70 lbs / 32 kgs for complimentary bags and 50 lbs / 23 kgs for excess charged bags
We calculate the size limits of your bag by adding the total outside dimensions of each bag, length + width + height.
More than one fee may apply per bag that exceeds standard dimensions for both weight and size. The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

(5) Limitation on basic standard deduction in the case of certain dependents

In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under section 151 is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall not exceed the greater of-
(B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income.
(6) Certain individuals, etc., not eligible for standard deduction
In the case of-
(A) a married individual filing a separate return where either spouse itemizes deductions,
(B) a nonresident alien individual, or
(D) an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership,
the standard deduction shall be zero.
(7) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025
In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026-
Paragraph (2) shall be applied-
(i) by substituting "$18,000" for "$4,400" in subparagraph (B), and
(ii) by substituting "$12,000" for "$3,000" in subparagraph (C).
(d) Itemized deductions
For purposes of this subtitle, the term "itemized deductions" means the deductions allowable under this chapter other than-
(1) the deductions allowable in arriving at adjusted gross income, and
(2) the deduction for personal exemptions provided by section 151.
(f) Aged or blind additional amounts
(1) Additional amounts for the aged
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he has attained age 65 before the close of his taxable year, and

(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse has attained age 65 before the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
(2) Additional amount for blind
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he is blind at the close of the taxable year, and
(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse is blind as of the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
For purposes of subparagraph (B), if the spouse dies during the taxable year the determination of whether such spouse is blind shall be made as of the time of such death.
(3) Higher amount for certain unmarried individuals
In the case of an individual who is not married and is not a surviving spouse, paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be applied by substituting "$750" for "$600".
(g) Marital status
For purposes of this section, marital status shall be determined under section 7703.

{"151": "§151. Allowance of deductions for personal exemptions

(a) Allowance of deductions

In the case of an individual, the exemptions provided by this section shall be allowed as deductions in computing taxable income.

(b) Taxpayer and spouse

An exemption of the exemption amount for the taxpayer; and an additional exemption of the exemption amount for the spouse of the taxpayer if a joint return is not made by the taxpayer and his spouse, and if the spouse, for the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins, has no gross income and is not the dependent of another taxpayer.

(c) Additional exemption for dependents

An exemption of the exemption amount for each individual who is a dependent (as defined in section 152) of the taxpayer for the taxable year.

(d) Exemption amount

For purposes of this section-

    (1) In general

    Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the term "exemption amount" means $2,000.

    (2) Exemption amount disallowed in case of certain dependents

    In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under this section is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the exemption amount applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall be zero.

    (3) Phaseout

        (A) In general

        In the case of any taxpayer whose adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b), the exemption amount shall be reduced by the applicable percentage.

        (B) Applicable percentage

        For purposes of subparagraph (A), the term "applicable percentage" means 2 percentage points for each $2,500 (or fraction thereof) by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b). In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, the preceding sentence shall be applied by substituting "$1,250" for "$2,500". In no event shall the applicable percentage exceed 100 percent.

    (5) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025

    In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026, the term "exemption amount" means zero.
", "2": "§2. Definitions and special rules

(a) Definition of surviving spouse

    (1) In general

    For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer-

        (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and

        (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151.

    For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual.

    (2) Limitations

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse-

        (A) if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, or

        (B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien.

(b) Definition of head of household

    (1) In general

    An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either-

        (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of-

            (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child-

                (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and

                (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or

            (ii) any other person who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such person under section 151, or

        (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151.

    For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual.

    (2) Determination of status

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1),

        (A) an individual who is legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married;

        (B) a taxpayer shall be considered as not married at the close of his taxable year if at any time during the taxable year his spouse is a nonresident alien; and

        (C) a taxpayer shall be considered as married at the close of his taxable year if his spouse (other than a spouse described in subparagraph (B)) died during the taxable year.

    (3) Limitations

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of this subtitle a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a head of a household-

        (A) if at any time during the taxable year he is a nonresident alien; or

        (B) by reason of an individual who would not be a dependent for the taxable year but for subparagraph (H) of section 152(d)(2).
", "7703": "§7703. Determination of marital status

(a) General rule

    (1) the determination of whether an individual is married shall be made as of the close of his taxable year; except that if his spouse dies during his taxable year such determination shall be made as of the time of such death; and

    (2) an individual legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married.

(b) Certain married individuals living apart

For purposes of those provisions of this title which refer to this subsection, if-

    (1) an individual who is married (within the meaning of subsection (a)) and who files a separate return maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of the taxable year the principal place of abode of a child with respect to whom such individual is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151,

    (2) such individual furnishes over one-half of the cost of maintaining such household during the taxable year, and

    (3) during the last 6 months of the taxable year, such individual's spouse is not a member of such household,

such individual shall not be considered as married.

support.text: (c) Standard deduction
(5) Limitation on basic standard deduction in the case of certain dependents

In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under section 151 is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall not exceed the greater of-
(B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income.
(6) Certain individuals, etc., not eligible for standard deduction
In the case of-
(A) a married individual filing a separate return where either spouse itemizes deductions,
(B) a nonresident alien individual, or
(D) an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership,
the standard deduction shall be zero.
(7) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025
In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026-
Paragraph (2) shall be applied-
(i) by substituting "$18,000" for "$4,400" in subparagraph (B), and
(ii) by substituting "$12,000" for "$3,000" in subparagraph (C).
(d) Itemized deductions
For purposes of this subtitle, the term "itemized deductions" means the deductions allowable under this chapter other than-
(1) the deductions allowable in arriving at adjusted gross income, and
(2) the deduction for personal exemptions provided by section 151.
(f) Aged or blind additional amounts
(1) Additional amounts for the aged
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he has attained age 65 before the close of his taxable year, and

(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse has attained age 65 before the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
(2) Additional amount for blind
The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-
(A) for himself if he is blind at the close of the taxable year, and
(B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse is blind as of the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
For purposes of subparagraph (B), if the spouse dies during the taxable year the determination of whether such spouse is blind shall be made as of the time of such death.
(3) Higher amount for certain unmarried individuals
In the case of an individual who is not married and is not a surviving spouse, paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be applied by substituting "$750" for "$600".
(g) Marital status
For purposes of this section, marital status shall be determined under section 7703.

{"151": "§151. Allowance of deductions for personal exemptions

(a) Allowance of deductions

In the case of an individual, the exemptions provided by this section shall be allowed as deductions in computing taxable income.

(b) Taxpayer and spouse

An exemption of the exemption amount for the taxpayer; and an additional exemption of the exemption amount for the spouse of the taxpayer if a joint return is not made by the taxpayer and his spouse, and if the spouse, for the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins, has no gross income and is not the dependent of another taxpayer.

(c) Additional exemption for dependents

An exemption of the exemption amount for each individual who is a dependent (as defined in section 152) of the taxpayer for the taxable year.

(d) Exemption amount

For purposes of this section-

    (1) In general

    Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the term "exemption amount" means $2,000.

    (2) Exemption amount disallowed in case of certain dependents

    In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under this section is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the exemption amount applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall be zero.

    (3) Phaseout

        (A) In general

        In the case of any taxpayer whose adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b), the exemption amount shall be reduced by the applicable percentage.

        (B) Applicable percentage

        For purposes of subparagraph (A), the term "applicable percentage" means 2 percentage points for each $2,500 (or fraction thereof) by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b). In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, the preceding sentence shall be applied by substituting "$1,250" for "$2,500". In no event shall the applicable percentage exceed 100 percent.

    (5) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025

    In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026, the term "exemption amount" means zero.
", "2": "§2. Definitions and special rules

(a) Definition of surviving spouse

    (1) In general

    For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer-

        (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and

        (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151.

    For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual.

    (2) Limitations

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse-

        (A) if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, or

        (B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien.

(b) Definition of head of household

    (1) In general

    An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either-

        (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of-

            (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child-

                (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and

                (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or

            (ii) any other person who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such person under section 151, or

        (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151.

    For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual.

    (2) Determination of status

    Notwithstanding paragraph (1),

        (A) an individual who is legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married;

        (B) a taxpayer shall be considered as not married at the close of his taxable year if at any time during the taxable year his spouse is a nonresident alien; and
